title: Compass watch: paging follow-ups and runbook TODOs
content:
Shift: Compass watch (06/12) 06:00-14:00
Owner: Imran Patel (imran) — short hand log, actionable followups

Topline:
- 3 pages during window; one SLO breach on embeddings-host-01 (high tail latency), two noisy alerts (kube-probe flaps).
- Incident for embeddings-host traced to a bad KV-cache eviction threshold after recent autoscaler bump. Temporary mitigation applied (rollback autoscaler config).
- Runbook gaps identified: missing explicit KV cache size check, unclear canary rollback steps for dedicated pool.

Pages (ordered):
1) 06:42 — embeddings-host-01 high token-latency (PagerDuty: PD-7892)
   - Symptoms: 95th pct token latency spiked from ~120ms -> 820ms for ~10m. 5% error ratio on stream timeouts.
   - Immediate actions: rolled back autoscaler bump (scale-down-threshold 0.6 -> 0.75) to previous value (MR 1123 reverted), drained one affected pod and re-queued long inflight requests.
   - Root-cause notes: autoscaler change reduced pod density which increased KV cache miss amplification for long-tail seqs; kernels saw more cold-cache loads.
   - Evidence: grafana panels (latency/kv-missrate/scheduler-loss) attached to incident.
   - Next: add a guard in autoscaler job to check average KV cache occupancy across pods before applying global change (see TODO A).

2) 08:15 — kube-apiserver probe flapping on node gcp-us-west-2b-07 (PD-7901)
   - Symptoms: Liveness probe failed intermittently ~3x / 5m; restarted kubelet container. Node stayed Ready. Many pods re-scheduled briefly causing minor 5xx spikes.
   - Quick triage: SSH to node, check /var/log/syslog — kernel OOM-killer log for containerd shim at 08:10. Container oom for exporter-sidecar. Not platform-wide.
   - Action: cordoned node, migrated user critical pods, filed infra ticket to cloud ops to inspect VM memory pressure (JIRA-5693).
   - Followup: add probe thresholds to avoid cascade restarts (see TODO B).

3) 11:55 — alert: long-running tail compaction on persistent volume pv-iops-11 (PD-7910)
   - Symptoms: compaction job took 2h > expected 20m, impacted local disk iops for a subset of replica sets.
   - Action: killed compaction, rescheduled for off-peak, increased rate limit for compactor process. Not a customer-facing outage.
   - Followup: schedule maintenance window and runbook entry for compaction jobs (TODO C).

Followups and Action Items (explicit):
- TODO A (high): Add KV cache occupancy check to autoscaler pipeline (owner: Imran). Steps:
  - Add metric 'kv_cache_avg_occupancy' to autoscaler heuristics (PR: infra/autoscaler#??).
  - If avg occupancy > 0.6, block aggressive scale-in or lower-burst policy.
  - Add unit tests + dry-run in staging before global rollout.
  - Target: patch + canary by 2026-06-16.

- TODO B (medium): Harden liveness probes and node-level guardrails (owner: Sofia)
  - Add probe backoff jitter and consecutive-failure thresholds for sidecars.
  - Add alert suppression window to prevent multiple PD pages for same node within 10m.
  - Linked ticket: JIRA-5693.

- TODO C (low): Compaction runbook & scheduled maintenance (owner: Ravi)
  - Create runbook steps: safe kill, resume, reschedule, contact list for owners.
  - Add rate-limits in compactor config to avoid saturating disk IOPS.
  - Add to quarterly maintenance calendar.

Runbook Gaps / Notes to self:
- KV-cache runbook lacks clear canary rollback sequence for Dedicated autoscaler changes (where to pin traffic, how to fall back to fallback-model-1). We need explicit steps and verification queries (p95 token-latency, kv-miss-rate).
- No checklist for when to cordon nodes vs drain vs reboot. Quick decision tree would help.
- Missing play for when compaction affects latency-sensitive LLM workloads; need escalation path to product-ops.

Quick commands / snippets I used (save for runbook):
- kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/autoscaler-config --to-revision=27  # rollback MR 1123
- kubectl drain gcp-us-west-2b-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- postgres psql -c "select count(*) from kv_cache where eviction_flag = true;"  # crude check
- curl -sS https://monitoring.internal/grafana/d/cpu-latency?panelId=12 | jq .

Notes on comms / timeline (for postmortem):
- 06:42 page -> initial mitigation 06:51 -> rollback complete 06:58 -> latency normalized by 07:05.
- Need timeline entries and who paged: oncall phone log shows page from PD at 06:42, acknowledged by me. Add to PM notes.

Unresolved questions / things to verify:
- Were any long-running requests dropped or returned truncated results during the spike? Need logs from proxy layer (ask log-team for filtered traces). (action: Imran)
- What was the observed KV cache hit ratio per pod before vs after autoscaler? (action: Sofia to extract)
- Is MR 1123 unsafe for small clusters (e.g., dev/dedicated pools)? Schedule a canary in dedicated-dev first.

Personal TODOs (in-shift quick list):
- Draft short incident blurb for standup (3 bullet summary).
- Open PR template for autoscaler guard (stubbed with tests).
- Add runbook checklist for compaction to Confluence page linked above.

Hand-off / next shift notes:
- Priority A: KV autoscaler guard — if no PR by EOD, ping me on slack #sre-ops.
- Priority B: Node memory pressure follow-up — cloud ops to report root cause; check JIRA-5693.
- Low: compaction runbook; schedule with Ravi next week.

Random scribbles / observations:
- Consider moving compactor to a dedicated low-iops class or throttling at kernel level.
- Maybe add a small local cache warmup on scale events to reduce cold-miss penalty (prototype idea).
- Remember: communicate rollback reasoning clearly to Dedicated customers if they ask — prepare short FAQ.

Appendix: Links and artifacts to attach in postmortem
- grafana: incidents/embed-01-latency (panel set)
- logs link: https://logs.internal/search?q=PD-7892
- MR revert: gitlab.com/redwood/infra/-/merge_requests/1123 (reverted)
- JIRA issues: JIRA-5689 (incident), JIRA-5693 (node mem), JIRA-5701 (compaction runbook)

End of notes.
